findings: OCC's Pooling Order Information distinguishes an application and respondent notice, hearing, and later prepared/signed and mailed order. The article asks readers to locate the actual order rather than calling a notice or application an issued order.

OCC's Electronic Case Filing page offers Case Document Search for documents and orders from March 21, 2022, while its legacy instructions direct earlier case information to Case Processing and archived imaging. The article does not invent newer client-rendered search fields or promise a complete case file.

OCC's Case Processing instructions define CD as Conservation Docket and relief code 41 as Pooling and describe the Link to Imaging. The article confines these to search labels, not owner-specific title evidence.

OCC Consumer Services describes its information-center remit for mineral and surface owners, including pooling and databases. The article uses it for record-location questions, not legal advice or a payor audit.

The title, description, answer summary, five FAQs, visible source links and body keep the same case-system distinction and expressly do not derive a personal election deadline or title/payment conclusion from the OCC overview.
